open_hypotheses: f9a44264 and 66f87cbc may both suffer from a format/salience issue — search loop entries are violated on every tested task (1042: 30+ loops, 221: 15+ loops). May need different trigger mechanism or placement.
The model may follow prohibitive instructions more rigidly than permissive overrides when they conflict — observed once on task 1042, needs more evidence.

EXECUTION_VARIANCE on task 221 (one rollout passed, one failed with same playbook) suggests the agent's application of checklist entries is stochastic. More prescriptive language at decision points may reduce variance.
The nested referent pattern ('book by author whose X happened') may be a common task family. If so, iter-3 update to 056f0a9e could have broad impact.
The train_pass jump (0.28→0.61) likely reflects batch composition more than playbook improvement — only 6 tasks per batch, different tasks sampled each iteration.
Consolidating f9a44264 and 66f87cbc into a single stronger entry might improve engagement vs. having two ignored entries.
preserve_until_more_evidence: 7ca56b8b [search_strategies] — validated helpful on 2 tasks (1042, 221). Only entry covering multi-clue decomposition. Strongest entry.

f9a44264 [query_formulation] — unique coverage for search axis flipping and document inspection. Agent hasn't followed it during loops but guidance is sound. Needs reformulation or more exposure, not deletion.
056f0a9e [answer_extraction] — iter-3 update with nested referent + biographical-beats-topical rules untested. Unique coverage for answer precision and commitment.
66f87cbc [common_mistakes] — unique coverage for verification loop detection. Not clearly engaged despite relevant loops on 2 tasks. Needs more exposure.
interference_patterns: f9a44264 ('change your search approach') and 66f87cbc ('stop searching and commit') prescribe different actions for the same trigger (repeated results). Agent doesn't follow either, so conflict is theoretical, but if engagement improves, sequencing may matter.
056f0a9e (answer checklist) and 66f87cbc (loop trap) both push toward commitment but from different cognitive phases (answer selection vs. search monitoring). Not observed to conflict.

questions: Why are f9a44264 and 66f87cbc not engaging during search loops? Is it formatting, trigger salience, or something about how the model processes instructions during extended search sequences?
Would a single consolidated loop-detection entry be more effective than two separate ones?
What other task families exist beyond multi-clue identification and nested-referent provenance? Broader task sampling needed.
Does the agent apply checklist entries more reliably at certain points in its reasoning (e.g., before answer vs. mid-search)?
notes: Two tasks studied in depth: 1042 (Conrad Anker, iters 1-2) and 221 (Barbara Hodgson, iter 3). 9/100 tasks seen total.
7ca56b8b is the most reliably helpful entry — multi-clue decomposition works across both studied task families.
Search loop problem is the most consistent recurring failure (confirmed on both tasks). Two entries designed for it but neither engages. This is the highest-priority gap.
EXECUTION_VARIANCE on task 221 suggests playbook entries need to be more prescriptive at decision points — advisory language may not be followed consistently.

scaffolding_effectiveness.ordered_procedure_steps: Agent follows 7ca56b8b's numbered procedure correctly. Procedural scaffolding effective for search strategy.

scaffolding_effectiveness.loop_interruption_format: Neither 'check every N searches' (66f87cbc) nor 'after 3+ searches with same results' (f9a44264) interrupted loops. This format may lack salience during extended search sequences.

recurring_failure_patterns: Repetitive search loops without strategic pivot — confirmed across tasks 1042 (30+ loops) and 221 (15+ loops). f9a44264 and 66f87cbc both designed for this but neither engages.
Answer commitment issues when some constraints unverifiable — task 1042: answer paralysis; task 221: fallback to surface match. Same root: agent lacks confidence to commit with partial verification.
